# SnapIt · Design System

---

## 0. Rulings — decided

*Was "Open rulings and flagged assumptions": four decisions made in the founder's absence and
held for a ruling. All four are ruled 2026-09-26 (D-081).*

| # | Assumption made | Ruling |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | **Logo direction A** (aperture bracket) locked as primary. Direction B (bracket + annotation stroke) built as an alternate. | **Ratified: Direction A is the mark.** Direction B was never committed and is not a sanctioned alternate — the annotation stroke brings an ink colour into the mark, which §10 Never forbids. |
| A2 | **Cobalt accent** taken from the portfolio palette; its owner was unknown. | **Settled by D-065 (2026-08-30):** the accent was rotated blue → cyan (`#006DAB` / `#00A4E4`, 202°) and snapit owns that slot in `_ops/HUE_REGISTER.md`. The ramp keeps the name *cobalt* in this document and the tokens; the name is a label, not a hue claim. |
| A3 | **Standalone brand, umbrella-ready.** | **Standalone. No extensions umbrella.** Token Track has its own locked identity (violet, Fira) and a different buyer; an umbrella would be a third brand to maintain for two products that never appear together. The `--snap-*` namespace stays. |
| A4 | **Name risk unresolved** (§1). | **Decided, conservative default — see §1.** Keep SnapIt; a clearance search gates the public store listing; the fallback name is fixed now so a conflict costs a re-outline, not a meeting. |

---

## 1. The name — and a standing risk

**SnapIt** — the product does one thing and the name says it.

> ⚠️ **Trademark risk — handling decided 2026-09-26 (D-081).** TechSmith's **Snagit** is the incumbent
> screenshot-and-annotation product and has been for two decades. "SnapIt" is
> one letter removed, in the identical product category, with identical
> function. This is the classic shape of a confusingly-similar mark. Chrome
> Web Store removal on a trademark complaint would cost the listing, the
> reviews, and the install base at once.
>
> **Required before any public listing:** Chrome Web Store search, USPTO TESS
> search, and a common-law search for existing "SnapIt" extensions. Nothing in
> this pack should reach a store listing until that clears.
>
> **The ruling:**
> 1. SnapIt stays the name through build and private testing.
> 2. The three searches above run before the Web Store listing is submitted — this is a gate in
>    the release checklist, not an open question.
> 3. **If any search returns a live conflict, or counsel judges the Snagit risk material, the
>    product ships as `Cropmark`** — the mark is literally a pair of crop marks, so the fallback
>    fits the identity with no change to anything but the wordmark cuts. `Cropmark` must pass
>    the same three searches.
> 4. Never register or use ® on either name without counsel. *Confirm with counsel before
>    filing.*
>
> The identity survives a rename. The mark carries no letterform, so only the wordmark
> cuts and the lockups need regenerating — by re-outlining, since they ship as paths.

---

## Overview

§2 · Brand essence

> **The capture frame, and nothing else in the way.**

A screenshot tool is infrastructure. It appears when summoned, does the thing,
and disappears. Every design decision here resolves to *getting out of the
way*: the UI floats over someone else's page and must never compete with it,
tint it, or obscure more of it than the job requires.

---

## 3. Personality

- **Primary:** the precise instrument. Exact, quiet, predictable. Pixel
  dimensions shown because they matter, not for decoration.
- **Secondary:** the tool that respects the page. Never a takeover, never a
  brand moment on someone else's content.
- **Personal-layer inheritance:** same root as Adommo and the Asif personal
  brand — restraint as confidence, evidence over adjectives.

**Not:** playful mascot utility · gamified prosumer app · AI-everything
screenshot "assistant" · loud freemium upsell surface.

---

## 4. Voice and tone

| Principle | Do | Don't |
|---|---|---|
| State, don't sell | "Capture region" | "Snap it in a flash!" |
| Numbers are the copy | "1284 × 620" | "Perfect size!" |
| Shortcuts over prose | `⌘ ⇧ 4` next to the action | "Press Command Shift Four to…" |
| No exclamation marks | "Copied" | "Copied to clipboard!" |

Sentence case everywhere. Verb-first on all actions. No terminal punctuation
on labels or buttons. Errors say what happened, then what to do.

---

## 5. Hard-nos

1. **No tinting the page.** The overlay scrim is neutral graphite at fixed
   alpha, never a coloured wash. This is the single most important rule.
2. No camera, scissors, or crop-tool clip art.
3. No gradient, glow, or glassmorphism on any chrome that floats over content.
4. No brand colour in the annotation ink set beyond the shared blue.
5. No watermark on exported captures, ever — not even on a free tier.

---

## 6. Visual principles

- **Neutral over warm.** The neutral ramp is cool graphite, not warm ash.
  Warm greys visibly tint whatever page they sit on; a screenshot tool cannot
  afford to shift the colour of the thing being screenshotted.
- **Dual-mode native, neither mode primary.** Chrome's toolbar theme is the
  user's choice, and the extension floats over both light and dark pages. Every
  asset ships in both, and the mark inherits `currentColor` so one file serves
  both toolbar themes.
- **Chrome is thin.** Hairlines (1px at 1×, 0.5px at ≥2× device pixel ratio), 6/8/12px radii
  (§16), no shadows except functional focus rings. *Pinned 2026-09-26 (D-081); was "0.5px
  hairlines, 6–12px radii".*
- **Mono carries the data.** Dimensions, coordinates, and keyboard shortcuts
  are always mono with tabular figures.

---

Applied theme: `theme.css`.

### Contrast — computed, not estimated

All 18 foreground/background pairings were measured with the WCAG 2.x relative
luminance formula. **Zero failures at AA body (<!-- AUTO:doc-ratio -->4.5:1<!-- /AUTO -->) for text pairings.** Non-text contrast (SC 1.4.11, 3:1) is verified separately — see `border-strong`. Verification data is
embedded in `tokens.json` under `contrast_verification`.

| Pairing | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|
| text on bg | 16.76 | 16.63 |
| text on surface | 17.96 | 13.24 |
| text-secondary on bg | 7.46 | 10.70 |
| text-secondary on surface | 8.00 | 8.52 |
| text-muted on bg | 4.93 | 6.24 |
| text-muted on surface | 5.29 | 4.97 |
| accent on bg | 6.30 | 6.10 |
| accent on surface | 6.76 | 4.86 |
| on-accent on accent | 6.76 | 6.10 |

**Print:** cobalt-300/400 fall outside CMYK gamut. For solids use cobalt-600
or 700, or a blue spot colour. Proof before press.

## 8. Annotation ink — a separate, functional palette

These are **not brand colours.** They are the pens the user draws with, and
they are chosen to be distinguishable from each other on arbitrary content.

| Ink | Hex | On white | On near-black |
|---|---|---|---|
| red | `#E5484D` | 3.91 | 4.94 |
| amber | `#FFB224` | 1.80 | 10.71 |
| green | `#46A758` | 3.03 | 6.37 |
| blue | `#00A4E4` | 3.17 | 6.10 |
| ink | `#14171C` | 17.96 | — |
| paper | `#FFFFFF` | — | 16.63 |

> **Mandatory halo rule.** Amber measures **<!-- AUTO:doc-ratio -->1.80:1<!-- /AUTO --> on white** — effectively
> invisible on a light screenshot. No recolouring fixes this, because ink is
> drawn over content whose colour is unknown at design time. Every annotation
> shape therefore carries a contrasting 1.5px outline via `paint-order: stroke
> fill` (`.snap-annotation` in `css/snapit_components.css`). This is a
> correctness requirement, not a style option — shipping ink without the halo
> makes the amber and green pens unusable on light pages.

## Typography

§9

Self-hosted, `fonts/fonts.css`. All SIL OFL 1.1.

| Role | Typeface | Weight |
|---|---|---|
| Display, headings, wordmark | **Geist** | SemiBold 600 |
| Body, UI | **Inter** | Regular 400 / Medium 500 |
| Dimensions, coordinates, keycaps | **Geist Mono** | Regular 400 / Medium 500 |

**Why this pairing.** No collision with the sibling brands: Adommo holds
Instrument Serif / Manrope / JetBrains Mono, the Asif personal brand holds IBM
Plex Mono / Sans. Geist is a neutral grotesque with no editorial character,
which is correct for a tool that must not editorialise over someone else's
page. The mono earns its place functionally — this product displays pixel
dimensions and keyboard shortcuts constantly, and both need tabular figures.

**Scale (px):** 11 · 12 · 13 · 14 · 16 · 18 · 22 · 28 · 36
**Line height:** tight 1.2 · normal 1.55 · relaxed 1.7
**Never** go below 11px. Extension popups are small; the answer is fewer
words, not smaller type.

## Layout

§14 · Layout and motion *(added 2026-09-26, D-081)*

SnapIt's surfaces are small and float over other people's pages, so the grid is 4px, not 8px.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Spacing grid | 4px — scale 4 / 8 / 12 / 16 / 20 / 24 / 32 / 48 |
| Popup | **320px** wide, height to content (max 480px); 12px padding; mode rows 44px |
| Capture toolbar | 40px tall, 32px buttons, 4px gap, 8px padding; sits 8px below the selection, flips above within 56px of the viewport bottom |
| Dimension readout | pinned 8px above the selection's top-left; flips inside when the selection touches the top edge |
| Options page | 720px max-width, single column, 32px section gap |
| Store / marketing page | 1080px max-width · 640 / 900 / 1200 px breakpoints |
| Touch target min | 32px on the in-page toolbar (pointer-driven) · 44px in the popup and options page |

### 14.1 Motion

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| duration-fast | 100ms | hover, focus, swatch select |
| duration-base | 160ms | toolbar appear, toast |
| easing | `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` | all |

The overlay scrim appears **instantly** — a fading scrim delays the capture gesture. No motion
on the selection rectangle itself. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` everything is instant.

---

## Elevation & Depth

§15 · Elevation *(added 2026-09-26, D-081)*

**No shadows** (§6, Hard-no 3). Chrome that floats over an unknown page cannot rely on a shadow
it can't predict, so it separates with a **two-ring edge** — the same logic as the annotation
halo (§8):

| Surface | Treatment |
|---|---|
| Floating toolbar, dimension readout, toast | `surface` fill + 1px `border-strong` inside + 1px outer ring in the opposite paper/ink (`#FFFFFF` on dark chrome, `#0C0E12` on light chrome) at 40% |
| Popup, options page cards | `surface` + 1px `border` — Chrome draws the popup frame |
| Wells, inputs | `surface-sunken` |
| Page scrim | `scrim` token, neutral graphite, fixed alpha — never tinted (Hard-no 1) |

---

## Shapes

§16 · Shape *(added 2026-09-26, D-081)*

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Corner radius | **6px** controls and swatches · **8px** toolbar, popup rows, toasts · **12px** store tiles, options cards · no pills |
| Selection rectangle | **0px** — the capture region is exact; its four 8px square handles are 1px `border` on `surface` |
| Border width | 1px (0.5px at ≥2× DPR for hairlines) · 2px selection stroke · 2px focus ring |

## Components

§17 · Component library specification *(added 2026-09-26, D-081 — extends §11 Product surfaces)*

Every component in light and dark, all states. §11 stays the source for the overlay rules and
the locked toolbar order.

### 17.1 Primitives
- **Buttons** — primary (accent fill, `on-accent` label), secondary (outline), ghost,
  icon-only (toolbar); 32px; default / hover / active / focus-visible / disabled.
- **Tool button** — icon-only, 32px, pressed state = `surface-sunken` + accent icon; tooltip
  with shortcut in Geist Mono.
- **Ink swatch** — 20px, 6px radius, halo ring (§8), selected = 2px accent ring with 2px gap.
- **Keycap** — Geist Mono 11px, `surface-sunken`, 1px `border`, 4px radius.
- **Toggle, checkbox, radio, select, text input** — all states.
- **Toast** — "Copied", "Saved to Downloads" — mono dimensions where relevant, 2s, no
  exclamation marks.

### 17.2 Capture surfaces
- **Scrim, selection rectangle, handles, dimension readout, annotation toolbar** — per §11.
- **Redact tool** — solid fill in `ink`, never blur (§11).
- **Text annotation** — Inter 16px default, halo applied.

### 17.3 Popup
- **Mode row** — icon, label, shortcut keycap right-aligned; bordered; hover and focus states.
- **First-run card** — the three shortcuts, "Got it" dismiss; shown once (§13).
- **Footer** — options link, version in mono.

### 17.4 Options page (closes the §13 component sheet)
Section cards: **Shortcuts** (rebind, with conflict warning) · **Capture** (default mode,
include cursor, file format PNG/JPEG, JPEG quality) · **Save** (copy to clipboard / download /
both, filename pattern with a live mono preview) · **Appearance** (light / dark / match Chrome) ·
**About** (version, licence, privacy note: "Nothing leaves your browser").

### 17.5 Microcopy inventory (closes the §13 microcopy pass)

| Situation | Copy |
|---|---|
| Popup, nothing captured this session | "Capture region, window or full page" |
| Restricted page (chrome://, Web Store) | "Chrome doesn't allow captures on this page. Try another tab." |
| Capture failed | "Capture failed. Reload the page and try again." |
| Clipboard blocked | "Couldn't copy. Download instead?" + Download button |
| Download blocked | "Downloads are blocked for this site. Copy instead?" |
| Selection too small | "Drag a larger area — at least 4 × 4" |
| Page too tall for full-page | "Page is taller than 16384px. Capturing the first 16384px." |
| Shortcut conflict | "⌘ ⇧ 4 is used by macOS. Choose another." |
| Copied / saved | "Copied" · "Saved to Downloads" |

Errors say what happened, then what to do. No "Oops", no exclamation marks (§4).

### 17.6 Iconography (closes §13 iconography)
**Lucide** (ISC licence), 1.5px stroke at 16px, `currentColor`. Toolbar mapping: rectangle
`square` · arrow `move-up-right` · freehand `pencil` · text `type` · redact `rectangle-horizontal`
(filled variant) · copy `copy` · download `download` · close `x`. No camera, scissors or crop
clip art (Hard-no 2).

## Do's and Don'ts

§18 · Do / Don't *(added 2026-09-26, D-081 — consolidates §4, §5, §6, §10)*

| ✅ Do | ❌ Don't |
|---|---|
| Keep the page scrim neutral graphite at fixed alpha | Tint the page with any colour |
| Separate floating chrome with the two-ring edge | Add a shadow, glow, gradient or glass effect over content |
| Put dimensions, coordinates and shortcuts in Geist Mono | Describe sizes in words ("Perfect size!") |
| Redact with a solid fill | Offer blur as a privacy affordance |
| Apply the halo to every annotation | Ship amber or green ink without it |
| Keep the accent on the selection rectangle inside the overlay | Put the brand accent on the mark inside the overlay |
| Export clean, at every tier | Watermark a capture, ever |
| Say "Copied" | Say "Copied to clipboard!" |

---

## 10. Logo

### Mark

Two opposing corner brackets. The negative space between them **is** the
capture region — the mark states the product's core gesture without depicting
a camera or a pair of scissors.

**Single-fill monochrome, always.** No dual-tone, no two-colour marks, ever.
All geometry is outlined to filled paths — there is no `stroke` attribute in
any shipped file, so the mark cannot break under non-uniform scaling.

### Two optical masters

A 16px toolbar icon and a 128px store icon are different design problems. The
first geometry (m 6.0 / R 3.5 / w 3.0 / L 3.0) measured **6.4% ink coverage**
at 16px with a 4px maximum row width — the mark effectively disappeared on a
Chrome toolbar. Parameters were swept against pixel-level measurement and two
masters were locked:

| Master | m | R | w | L | Coverage @ target | Used at |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| display | 5.2 | 3.8 | 3.8 | 4.2 | 12.9% | 48px and above, all lockups, web |
| small | 4.8 | 4.0 | 4.6 | 5.0 | 17.8% | 16px and 32px icons, favicons |

Where `m` = arm centreline inset, `R` = corner radius, `w` = stroke weight,
`L` = arm length beyond the corner, all in a 32-unit viewBox. Exact paths and
parameters: `geometry_lock.json`.

### Wordmark

"SnapIt" outlined from **Geist SemiBold** via HarfBuzz shaping with kerning
applied. No live text, no font dependency. Measured advance 3130 units at
1000 upem; cap height 726.

### Lockups

- **Horizontal (primary).** Mark ink height = **1.32 × cap height**, gap =
  **0.30 × cap height**, mark centred on the wordmark's cap-height midline.
- **Stacked.** Mark ink height = **2.20 × cap**, gap = **0.38 × cap**,
  centred.

Both scale the mark by its **ink bounds**, not its nominal 32-unit box. The
mark's arms are inset, so box-scaling renders it roughly 18% undersized — an
error caught in visual QA and corrected.

### Clearspace and minimum sizes

- **Clearspace:** one corner-radius unit (R at the active master) on all sides.
- **Minimum:** mark 16px · horizontal lockup 96px wide · stacked 64px wide.

### Never

Stretch or scale non-uniformly · recolour outside graphite/cobalt · add
shadow, glow, or gradient · place on busy or photographic backgrounds ·
rebuild the wordmark in another typeface · fill the mark with an annotation
ink colour · apply the brand accent to the mark inside the capture overlay
(the accent there belongs to the selection rectangle).

---

## 11. Product surfaces

**Capture overlay.** Neutral scrim over the page. Selection rectangle in
2px accent with four corner handles. Live dimension readout in mono, pinned
above the selection's top-left. Floating annotation toolbar below the
selection, flipping above when the selection sits near the viewport bottom.

**Toolbar order (locked):** rectangle · arrow · freehand · text · redact ·
divider · ink swatches · divider · primary action.

**Redaction is not a blur.** Redact fills solid; blur is reversible in
principle and should never be offered as a privacy affordance.

**Popup panel.** Three capture modes as bordered rows, each with its keyboard
shortcut in mono, right-aligned. No hero, no illustration, no upsell.

**Empty and error states.** "Nothing captured yet" is banned. Name the space
and give the verb.

---

## 13. Items — all resolved

*Was "Open items". Closed 2026-09-26 (D-081).*

- **Rulings A1–A4** — ruled in §0.
- **Microcopy inventory** — §17.5.
- **Iconography** — §17.6: Lucide, named, with the toolbar mapping.
- **Monetisation and onboarding** — **free, no account, no paid tier at launch.** Capture,
  annotate, redact, copy and download are free forever and never watermarked (Hard-no 5). Any
  later paid tier may add cloud share links only; it may never gate a capture or an export.
  Onboarding is therefore **one dismissible first-run card** in the popup listing the three
  shortcuts — no tour, no account prompt (§17.3).
- **Options/settings page component sheet** — §17.4.

**Stability:** identity stable for at least a year from 2026-09-26; changes go through a dated
amendment here.

**Priority note:** per operating principle 11, this build does not outrank
outreach on the revenue path.

## Logo colour — amended 2026-09-02

**Founder ruling: the logo and mark carry the brand colour.** The shipped assets were monochrome
ink, which left the brand's own hue absent from its identity.

The mark takes the accent — `#006DAB` on light, `#00A4E4` on dark. **The wordmark stays ink.**
That half of the rule is unchanged and near-universal in this portfolio: a wordmark filled with
an accent loses contrast, and the mark is where colour earns its keep.

The prior monochrome constraint is **retired, not overruled quietly**. What it was protecting —
that the mark must survive one-colour reproduction — is preserved: `currentColor` and
single-fill cuts remain available for embossing, thermal print and one-ink contexts.


> **`usage-sheet.html` — added 2026-09-02.** Every brand now ships one: side-by-side
> DO / DON'T panels for logo and mark placement, rendered from the committed SVGs against
